chunks: From him, from Fadala, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has one hundred dinars with the money-changer, and the money-changer has one thousand dirhams with him, so they exchange them against each other. He said, 'There is no harm with it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to offset debts in different currencies between a customer and a money-changer?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical application of *qita'* (set-off) in early Islamic commercial law, specifically addressing the complexity of cross-currency debt settlement between a depositor and a *sarraf* (money-changer). Imam al-Sadiq’s affirmation of permissibility highlights the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in accommodating diverse monetary systems, ensuring that differing currencies do not obstruct the resolution of mutual obligations. This ruling underscores the principle that as long as the underlying debts are valid, the method of settlement can adapt to the specific assets held by each party.
